name: Lamech
charge: Killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance
summary: Lamech of Cain's line told his wives Adah and Zillah of a killing and claimed seventy-sevenfold vengeance for himself against Cain's sevenfold. His declaration is preserved without a separate sentence executed upon him. Protection pronounced by God over Cain had become a man's boast about his own vengeance.
offense: Lamech of Cain's line took two wives, Adah and Zillah, and addressed them concerning a man he had slain to his wounding and a young man to his hurt (Genesis 4:19,23). His speech culminated in a claim of vengeance: if Cain were avenged sevenfold, Lamech would be seventy and sevenfold (Genesis 4:24). The protection God had pronounced over Cain became the measure of his own boast. God had restrained others from killing Cain; Lamech spoke as though that restraint authorized an even greater claim for himself. He made no recorded appeal for repentance or forgiveness. Vengeance was being treated as a man's possession to enlarge, although the Lord declares that vengeance belongs to him (Deuteronomy 32:35). A divine limit upon retaliation cannot rightly be turned into permission to threaten more of it.
judgment: Genesis gives no separate sentence executed upon this Lamech. His speech is preserved as testimony to the violence and self-exaltation within Cain's genealogy, before the account turns to Seth and those who called upon the Lord (Genesis 4:23-26). The absence of a narrated punishment does not make his claim God's promise. Romans 12:19 commands the hearer not to avenge himself but to leave recompense to the Lord. Lamech's seventy-sevenfold is his own declaration; it is not the Lord extending Cain's protection by a new command.

verses.text: And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.

text.text: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.
And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.

lawDetails.text: Avenge not yourselves, for vengeance is in God's hands.
All boasting and bragging is wicked.
The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

entries.commentary: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at [Genesis 3:21](/bible/genesis/3#v21). If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him.
When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.
Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3.

Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in [Genesis 1](/bible/genesis/1), that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. When you read about the sons of God in [Genesis 5](/bible/genesis/5) you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked.
An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created.

Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. The song opens by calling heaven and earth to witness, just as Moses said in chapter 31. Notice how the verses run together: my doctrine shall drop as the rain, and then, because I will publish the name of the Lord. Doctrine and the name go together, and greatness is ascribed unto our God.

He is the Rock, his work is perfect, all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he. The song gives the Most High his praise first, then turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves. They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land. Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? Hath he not made thee, and established thee? Isaiah recounts the lovingkindness of the Most High toward the house of Israel: he said, surely they are my people, children that will not lie, so he was their Savior. In all our affliction he was afflicted; whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us, and in his love and in his pity he redeemed us and carried us all the days of old. How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee. Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you. The men teaching on the corners and bringing out these prophecies and breakdowns are the ones Moses said would teach you these things: ask thy father, and he will shew thee. Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers: study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers; that is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves. Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. You thought God wants everybody to just come together and hold hands? The God of this Bible has been a God of division from day one; he separated the sons of Adam according to where he had to place the children of Israel, meaning this world revolves around Israel. For the Lord's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. In the division of the nations he set a ruler over every people, but Israel he kept for himself: that is my inheritance, that is my portion.

He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye. The same people the world counted as three fifths of a man are the apple of the Most High's eye. Zechariah shows who that people is: deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Who was held captive in the land of the north, in North America, but the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans? We are Zion, and we must deliver ourselves from the ways we were taught there. He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye: the nations that spoiled Israel and did her harm have a grand payback coming when Christ returns.

As an eagle stirreth up her nest and beareth her young on her wings, so the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him. The Most High used no idol of wood or stone to lead us through the wilderness and protect us from the nations; he did that alone. He made him ride on the high places of the earth, to eat the increase of the fields, honey out of the rock, butter of kine and milk of sheep, the fat of lambs and rams, and the pure blood of the grape. This is the journey through the wilderness, how Israel came through all those nations and acquired wealth and provision from the Most High's own hand.

But Jeshurun, meaning Israel, waxed fat, and kicked; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. Waxing fat is not about being overweight; [Deuteronomy 8](/bible/deuteronomy/8) explains it. When thou hast eaten and art full, and hast built goodly houses, and thy herds and thy silver and thy gold are multiplied, then thine heart is lifted up and thou forgettest the Lord thy God which brought thee out of the house of bondage. With all the resources the Most High provided, we started to act like it was us: we got all this money, we were on the grind, we made it happen. No, it was God; we get blessed and act like it was not a blessing from the Most High.

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods; they sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not. What are examples of new gods? Islam came about in 622 AD, some six hundred years after Christ. The familiar image of Christ painted in the Renaissance era is a new thing under the sun. Even Buddha, whom people think is ancient, came on the scene between the sixth and fourth centuries BC; our kingdom had already been split and carried captive into Babylon before anybody heard of a Buddha. These are new gods that our people go crazy over today, and the Most High said we would come to that estate.

Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee. When it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful. Who is that Rock? Paul says our fathers drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses; he was with Israel in the wilderness. David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

When the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons and of his daughters; he said, I will hide my face from them, for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. This goes especially into Judah, the southern kingdom: when Christ was on the scene, the scribes and Pharisees rejected him; they were very froward and had no faith that he was the Son of God, and Christ called them a generation of vipers. They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God, and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people. Some close the book right there and say the Most High welcomed all the other nations in place of Israel; no, the ones which are not a people are also Israel. Isaiah says within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and Hosea says of the northern kingdom, ye are not my people, yet in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

For a fire is kindled in mine anger; I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them: burning hunger, bitter destruction, and the teeth of beasts sent upon them. You have seen the clips from the civil rights movement, the canines sent at our people to rip at them with their teeth. That was a fulfillment of prophecy: the Most High said he would send the teeth of beasts against us. The sword without, and terror within, destroying young man and virgin, the suckling with the man of gray hairs: the sword of the other nations, and famine and drought as well. This prophecy had to happen against us because we served other gods.

I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. What corners? Isaiah shows the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth: the scattering was worldwide. What nation of people has been scattered throughout the four corners of the earth by slave trades, the transatlantic, the sub-Saharan, the silk road? The so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. This never happened to the people claiming our heritage; it is further proof of who the children of Israel are. The nations we were scattered to took counsel together: come, let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. Divide them, teach them they are not who they really are: if I get them to take pride in being called anything but Israel, they will never remember. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, but the remembrance has not completely ceased.

Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this. The Most High would not let the enemy think they accomplished the complete destruction of the Israelites by their own hand; that is why, after a certain amount of time, he begins waking us up, and why we are starting to remember who we are this day. For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them. O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end. If you knew exactly what disaster was coming and when, you would set every alarm; our forefathers were told all these atrocities ahead of time and still did not consider it. How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up? How could we be conquered the way we were, thousands rounded up by a few, unless the Most High allowed it? It had to be the Lord.

For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges. For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: that is why the sins of Sodom show up among our people today, even paraded as pride. The Most High said our vine became the vine of Sodom; their grapes are grapes of gall, their wine is the poison of dragons. Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures? These prophecies were sealed up with the Most High until their time.

To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand. After he let these nations deceive and oppress us for so long, the Most High will show who God really is; but he had to let us humble ourselves first for serving all those false gods. For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants: he will change his mind, and instead of inflicting wrath upon us he will save us. When he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left: when he sees that we have fallen to our lowest estate possible, then he moves.

And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted? Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you. The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us. Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand. A statue you made with your hands cannot kill a thing and cannot make alive; the true God does both. That is the terrible God we serve, the God of our people, and once his people get back on his good side, the nations that touched the apple of his eye have judgment coming.

For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever. The Most High will eventually turn back to save us; he will stop hiding his face and come to our defense. If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me. I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy. The Most High takes revenge for the captives, because he is the God of the people that have been in captivity over and over again. In the churches they never read this; they never knew that God is this way, and it shows what they really think about him.

Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people. Read through the Bible: Christ put to death, James put to death, Peter put to death, and since the Bible was written more prophets have lost their lives for the truth, and it will continue. The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto the Most High, and the souls of the just complain continually, asking when he will act; and he answers, I will surely avenge them. This is fulfilled in the destruction of Babylon: rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets, for God hath avenged you on her. Babylon the great in this teaching is the United States of America; that is where the Lord makes his arrows drunk with blood, the vengeance promised for all the wrong these nations have done unto us.

Moses and Joshua spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, and Moses said, Set your hearts unto all the words which I testify among you this day, which ye shall command your children to observe to do. For it is not a vain thing for you; because it is your life. The words of this law are not something to sit on your dashboard or in your cabinet; this book is your life, and if you are not reading it, you are not living. Through this thing ye shall prolong your days in the land: not just eating right or exercising, but doing this law is how you prolong your days.

That selfsame day the Most High tells Moses: get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan; and die in the mount, as Aaron died in mount Hor, because ye trespassed against me at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel. The account is in Numbers 20: the people angered Moses at the waters of strife, complaining and provoking him after all they had already seen, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes. They provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips: Hear now, ye rebels; and he smote the rock twice instead of speaking to it, the Rock we read about earlier in this chapter. Thou shalt see the land before thee; but thou shalt not go thither.
